params.place: on the map: the globe diving to the South Atlantic, Tristan da Cunha alone in it

moments.what: the globe already turning as the camera dives toward the South Atlantic
the empty ocean fills the frame, rings of waves around one dot
the island's volcano outline draws itself and TRISTAN DA CUNHA writes on
a pin drops onto the island with a ping
a big question mark bounces up beside it
tiny house roofs pop on the island's north shore
the pin pulses

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Tristan da Cunha: the most remote island anyone lives on. Who settled here?

params.place: on the map: the South Atlantic from Saint Helena to Cape Town

moments.what: the camera pulls back from Tristan
a ruler line starts north from Tristan
Saint Helena's island pops up far to the north
its name writes on
the distance sign rises beside the ruler
the ruler's end pulses at Saint Helena
South Africa traces itself and fills with its flag
a second ruler line runs east toward Cape Town
the second distance sign rises
Cape Town's pin drops
the camera settles wide on both lines

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its nearest neighbour, Saint Helena, sits 2,430 km to the north, and South Africa is 2,816 km away to the east.

params.place: on the map: Cape Town's harbour and the sea lane to Tristan

moments.what: a plane icon flies toward the island and is stamped out with a red cross
a runway strip on the island is crossed out
the camera swings east to Cape Town
a supply ship leaves the Cape Town pin
a calendar sign flips its days as the ship sails
the ship's wake draws across the ocean
the ship reaches the island

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: There's no airport and no runway. To get here, you sail for about a week from Cape Town.

params.place: on the map: Tristan close, its north shore and the volcano

moments.what: the island fills the middle of the frame, its cone rising
a village sign plants on the north shore with the head count
little houses pop along the strip of flat land
the sea and the cliffs press in from both sides
the volcano's peak puffs a small cloud
the surf rings pulse in against the shore
potato patches stripe the slope behind the village
a fishing boat with a lobster pot bobs off the shore

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Yet 222 people live here, in one village squeezed between the sea and a volcano, growing potatoes and fishing for lobster.

params.place: on the map: the sea lane north from Tristan to Saint Helena

moments.what: a question mark hops off the island
the camera starts gliding north over the ocean
a magnifying glass slides over the sea
Saint Helena comes into the lens
Saint Helena glows under the glass

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So why here at all? The clue is on that neighbour to the north.

params.place: on the map: Europe at Waterloo down the Atlantic to Saint Helena

moments.what: Europe on the map, a crossed swords mark at Waterloo
the swords break and Belgium's border traces
Napoleon (his real face) appears on the map at Waterloo
a British ship takes him and sails south down the Atlantic
the ship reaches Saint Helena
Napoleon stands on the tiny island behind a fence
the camera pulls back to show Europe far away
a crown pops over his head
France and its neighbours tint blue

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: After losing at Waterloo, Napoleon, the French emperor who had ruled much of Europe, was locked away on Saint Helena, a speck of rock far from Europe.

params.place: on the map: Saint Helena and Tristan, the sea between them

moments.what: the Union flag pops over Saint Helena
a French ship appears in the open sea
Tristan sits almost bare, one lone hut on it
a dashed red route runs from Tristan up to Saint Helena, the French ship on it
a British ship sails to Tristan, redcoats on deck
a Union flag plants on Tristan with the year on a sign
the dashed rescue route snaps and fades
Napoleon's head appears on Saint Helena
the British ship sets off from the Cape

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Britain feared the French would use nearly empty Tristan to rescue him. So in 1816, it sent soldiers and claimed the island.

params.place: on the map: Tristan's north shore, ships leaving and arriving

moments.what: the garrison's ship loads up at the shore
it sails away north off the frame
one small figure stays on the shore
William Glass, his wife and children stand by a hut, a name label writes on
a hut pops up beside them
small boats sail in from the west
more huts pop along the shore
a signpost plants in the village
EDINBURGH writes on the signpost
OF THE SEVEN SEAS writes under it
his wife and children step up beside him
the boats land at the shore
the huts' roofs brighten
the camera eases back to the signpost

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: When the soldiers left, one corporal, William Glass, asked to stay with his family. Sailors and settlers joined them, and their village got a grand name: Edinburgh of the Seven Seas.

params.place: on the map: Tristan erupting, then the long route north to England

moments.what: the island shakes
lava and a tall ash cloud burst from the side of the cone
a sign with the number of islanders lifts off the village
a ship carrying the islanders sails north up the Atlantic
the route lands on England, a pin drops
the lava runs down toward the village houses
the houses shake as the lava nears
the islanders gather on the shore

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then the volcano erupted right beside the village, and all 264 islanders were shipped to England.

params.place: on the map: England down the Atlantic to Tristan

moments.what: the ship turns at England
houses on the map of England stay grey
the ship sails the whole Atlantic south
it reaches Tristan and the village lights come back on
a grey cloud rains over the English houses
Tristan glows far to the south

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But in England most of them missed home, and they chose to sail all the way back.

params.place: on the map: Saint Helena and Tristan together, the line between them

moments.what: the islanders stand along the shore, the head count sign beside them
Tristan's village glows in the empty ocean
the camera rises over the South Atlantic
Napoleon's face lights up on Saint Helena far to the north
a bright line ties Saint Helena to Tristan
a door sign NEXT DOOR stamps on the line

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So 222 people live on the loneliest island on Earth because one prisoner was once locked up next door.

params.place: on the map: the camera rising to the globe and diving back to Tristan

moments.what: Saint Helena's pin pulses
the camera swings west and a Pitcairn pin pops far off in the Pacific
both pins bob
the map turns into the globe
a comment bubble pops beside the globe
the globe turns back toward the South Atlantic
Tristan's outline draws itself again, as in the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Saint Helena or Pitcairn: which lonely island should we map next? Tell me below, and look again at Tristan da Cunha.
